docs/architecture/key-files/core-utilities-2.md:29:- `src/core/runtime-version.ts` — Bun 1.4.4 minimum (`MINIMUM_BUN_VERSION`; 1.4.0-1.4.2 leak every chunk a postgres.js TLS connection reads, #7644 #7596). `unsupportedBunMessage` names the found and required versions and the fix (`bun upgrade`, restart, `gbrain post-upgrade` for an interrupted upgrade). `exitOnUnsupportedBun` is the CLI entrypoint gate: every command below the floor exits 1 before dispatch (`--version` still prints, exit 0, so an older gbrain's upgrade can verify the swap; `autopilot` also writes the refusal to stdout, its service log); the guarded HTTP transport asserts it; doctor reports it as `bun_runtime`. Package engines, runtime checks and the CI Bun matrices share the same floor (`test/scripts/ci-pr-scope.test.ts`). `compareBunVersions`/`bunVersionMeets` order Bun versions by semver (a `-canary` prerelease sits below its release; `+revision` metadata is ignored), shared with the upgrade floor gate. `SECURE_BUN_VERSION` (1.4.4) is the first Bun with the Brotli fix for CVE-2026-111497 (#7373): the floor is not below it, so a runtime without the fix is refused; doctor's `bun_runtime` warns (`gbrain upgrade` for a standalone binary, `bun upgrade` for a bun install) only for a supported runtime below it, and the CI primary pin may not drop below it (`test/scripts/ci-pr-scope.test.ts`).
docs/architecture/key-files/commands-6.md:16:- Release channels: `src/core/self-upgrade.ts` resolves the channel (`resolveReleaseChannel`: `--channel`, `GBRAIN_RELEASE_CHANNEL`, `self_upgrade.channel`, default `stable`; `latest` normalizes to `alpha`; an invalid value at the first present source is an error) and keeps the update cache (`update-check.<channel>.json`, tagged with the evidence policy; an older answer never overwrites a newer one, unless the stored check time is more than 5 minutes ahead of the clock, and a cache file dated more than 5 minutes ahead is stale, so a clock that moved back never freezes the cache (#8795)) and the time-based snooze (`update-snoozed.<channel>.json`) per channel; `offeredVersion` never offers a downgrade except to move off a `known_bad` version. `src/core/stable-channel.ts` reads and strictly parses the evidence record (`stable.json` on `stable-record`; `requiredEvidenceKeys`: `soak_run`, plus `matrix_run` from `MATRIX_REQUIRED_FROM`), maps failures to `stable_missing` / `stable_invalid` / `stable_unreadable` with sanitized causes, and `resolveStableRelease` checks the `stable` and `v<version>` tags against the record commit. `src/commands/upgrade-channel.ts` plans an upgrade's target (`channelTarget`, `runUpgradeDryRun` for `gbrain upgrade --dry-run --json`) and refuses with the typed code. `src/commands/check-update.ts` `refreshUpdateCache` never reads a bare VERSION for stable and never falls back to alpha. `src/core/release-channel-notice.ts` prints the one-time `[gbrain notice release_channel]` line on stderr (marker file under `notices/`; not under `--json`, `serve` or `mcp`; only when no channel is set). `src/core/install-ref.ts` is the one ref every install surface names, linted by `scripts/check-install-ref.ts`. Tests: `test/release-channel-w1.serial.test.ts`, `test/upgrade-stable-channel.test.ts`, `test/install-ref.test.ts`. Docs: `docs/guides/upgrades-auto-update.md#stable-channel`.
docs/architecture/key-files/ci-health-and-test-guards.md:7:- `.github/workflows/upgrade-matrix.yml` + `scripts/upgrade-matrix.ts` (modules in `scripts/upgrade-matrix/`) — upgrade-from-N matrix (GBRA-224 W2). `plan` resolves the candidate and from-versions (N-1, N-10, N-50, 30 days, stable, and `stable-window`: `versions.ts` `stableWindow` over the `stable-v*` record tags, the newest 8 plus one per older month back 183 days) from release tags; `cell` installs a from-version with `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain` in an isolated HOME, seeds a brain, runs that release's `gbrain upgrade` against `github-fixture.ts` (per-cell bare mirror via git `insteadOf`, loopback tarball API, TLS fixture behind `HTTPS_PROXY`; every other host refused), then checks install identity, one build across a running serve, apply-migrations, schema head, doctor, canonical preservation (`snapshot.ts`), writes, keyed vector query on the mock provider and the old binary on the upgraded brain; `summarize` judges red/hold/green (`verdict.ts`, `known-exceptions.json`, the `W4 SWITCH POINT` for `doctor --alert`); `issue` keeps one `upgrade-break` issue with `marker.ts`'s `ISSUE_MARKER` and a `red-from` line naming the failing from-versions. Tests: `test/scripts/upgrade-matrix.test.ts`. Docs: `docs/ci-upgrade-matrix.md`.
docs/architecture/key-files/ci-health-and-test-guards.md:14:- `.github/workflows/promote-stable.yml` + `scripts/promote-stable.ts` — stable channel promotion (`workflow_dispatch`: `version`, `soak_run_url`, `matrix_run_url`, `scoreboard_url`, `rollback`, `reason`, `withdraw`, `not_promotable`, `not_promotable_reason`, `not_promotable_fixed_in`, `not_promotable_remove`; concurrency group `promote-stable`). `promote()` refuses unless the actor's `role_name` is admin or maintain (`authorize()`; the one exception is `PromoteDeps.scheduled`, set by `scheduleAuthorized()` only for a schedule event of `stable-daily.yml` on the default branch, which also requires the release commit on master and records `promoted_by: schedule (.github/workflows/stable-daily.yml)`), `v<VERSION>` exists with a `VERSION` file naming it and a published (non-draft) GitHub release, the soak run URL names a completed, successful run of this repository's `STABLE_SOAK_WORKFLOW` workflow (repository variable; bare file name or path), the run's head commit has the release tag's exact tree (fetched when missing), `checkMatrix()` accepts the named upgrade matrix run only through `scripts/stable-matrix.ts` `judgeMatrixRun()` (a completed schedule or dispatch run of master's harness, full profile, no fault, whose `upgrade-matrix-receipt` names the release's tag, commit and tree and the run's own harness, and green; a scheduled promotion must name one, a maintainer may not and the record says `matrix_run: null`), and the version is newer than the current stable (the highest `v*` tag on `refs/tags/stable^{commit}`), or older with `rollback` and a reason. Re-promoting the current stable (no rollback) moves no tag: `recordCurrentStable()` writes `stable.json` from the stable tag's message (`parseTagMessage()`, which must name the same commit, tree and soak run) when the published record does not name that release, leasing `stable` unchanged and the record branch, and refuses as a no-op otherwise (GBRA-346 backfill for releases promoted before the record existed). It creates the immutable annotated `stable-v<VERSION>` record (refused when it exists, except on a rollback re-promotion of the same commit) and moves the annotated `stable` tag, both with `renderTagMessage()`'s `key: value` body, commits the evidence record (`renderRecord()`, `stable.json`, `known_bad` carried forward and merged with `withdraw` by `mergeKnownBad()`, `not_promotable` carried forward, added to and removed from by `mergeNotPromotable()`, which caps a reason at 500 characters; a record over `STABLE_RECORD_MAX_BYTES`, the client's `RECORD_MAX_BYTES`, is refused before the push) on the `stable-record` branch, then pushes all three in one `--atomic` push (`stable` and `stable-record` leased on the values it read, so a failed push changes nothing) and writes the step summary. Side effects come in through `PromoteDeps`. Tests: `test/scripts/promote-stable.test.ts`. Docs: `docs/RELEASING.md#stable-channel-promotion`.
docs/architecture/key-files/ci-health-and-test-guards.md:26:- `scripts/ci-install-openclaw.sh` — e2e.yml's Tier 2 `Install OpenClaw` step. Each `npm install -g openclaw@<pin>` attempt is bounded (`timeout 120`); a failure whose npm log carries `code ETARGET` or `E404` is a registry race (a dependency version published but not yet visible for every package of its release, the 2026-10-12 master Tier 2 red on `@aws-sdk/credential-provider-node@^3.972.86`) and is retried up to 4 attempts 20/40/80 s apart; any other failure keeps the 3 attempts 10 s apart. Nothing else is retried, and the last attempt fails the step with npm's own log. Knobs (`OPENCLAW_SPEC`, `OPENCLAW_INSTALL_ATTEMPT_S`, `OPENCLAW_INSTALL_RETRY_SLEEP_S`, `OPENCLAW_INSTALL_RACE_SLEEPS_S`) exist for the test: `test/scripts/ci-install-openclaw.test.ts` installs a one-file package from a loopback registry (`test/helpers/npm-stub-registry.ts`) that answers ETARGET or E404 to the first three packument requests, forever, or publishes for an impossible `os` (`EBADPLATFORM`, the generic path). The lockfile route (a committed `package-lock.json` per pin) was weighed and not taken: two pins live in the workflows (`e2e.yml` 2026.4.9, `native-locks.yml` 2026.9.4), every bump would regenerate a multi-hundred-kilobyte lockfile, and the race the retry waits out is a propagation delay of minutes.
docs/architecture/key-files/core-utilities-1.md:67:- `src/core/npm-squat-check.ts` — doctor's `npm_squat`: classifies `gbrain` on PATH plus `npm root -g` and Bun global packages. Foreign winner: ask_user remove (npm/bun only from its own global dir, else the user's step); `#stable` + #218 only when no gbrain is left. Windows: MSYS paths, `.exe`. Tests: `npm-squat-check`, `doctor-npm-squat`.
docs/architecture/key-files/entrypoints-and-docs.md:14:- `admin/` — React 19 + Vite + TypeScript admin SPA embedded in the binary via `admin/dist/` served by `serve-http.ts`. Views: Login (bootstrap token or single-use link → session cookie, preserving pending OAuth consent), Dashboard (metrics + SSE feed + token health), Agents (client table + registration), Register (machine/public PKCE/confidential PKCE with permission preview), Client Setup (method-aware instructions + explicit recoverable private download), Request Log (filterable paginated), Agent Detail drawer (setup, permission review, request activity, and token invalidation/revocation/deletion). Design tokens: `#0a0a0f` bg, Inter for UI, JetBrains Mono for data, 4-32px spacing scale, rounded pill badges. HTTP-only SameSite=Strict cookie auth. About 79KiB gzip for JS/CSS assets. Build: `cd admin && bun install && bun run build`; output at `admin/dist/` is committed for self-contained binaries.

content.text:
# Install

> [!TIP]
> **Fastest: hosted GBrain at [gbrain.io](https://gbrain.io/cli?ref=install-md), for any harness.** One command launches a GBrain hosted on gbrain.io; Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT, Cursor and every other AI you use connect to it, with nothing to keep online.
>
> ```bash
> curl -sSL https://gbrainio.terminalwire.sh | bash
> gbrainio terminal connect      # in a new terminal
> gbrainio workspace new         # pick a plan in the browser
> curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash   # skip if Bun 1.4.4+ is installed
> export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"
> bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable   # the gbrain CLI only; no local brain
> # Claude Code (an existing gbrain entry is kept):
> (claude mcp get gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1 || claude mcp add --transport http --scope user gbrain https://gbrain.io/mcp) && gbrain setup claude-code --instructions-only
> # Codex (an existing gbrain entry is kept):
> (codex mcp get gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1 || codex mcp add gbrain --url https://gbrain.io/mcp) && gbrain setup codex --instructions-only
> ```
>
> Bun's installer needs `unzip` and stops with `error: unzip is required to install bun` without it. Check with `command -v unzip`; if it prints nothing, install it first: `apt-get update && apt-get install -y unzip` (Debian, Ubuntu), `dnf install -y unzip` (Fedora, RHEL) or `apk add unzip` (Alpine), with `sudo` in front unless you are root. No way to install packages? Use the [no-unzip route](../INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md#no-unzip), not an improvised one.
>
> `gbrain setup <harness> --instructions-only` tells the agent the brain is there; agents seldom call an MCP server nobody told them about. It writes the [brain-first block](guides/setup.md#brain-first-instructions) into `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` or Codex's `AGENTS.md` (a non-empty `AGENTS.override.md` instead when Codex has one) with a per-turn rule hook, and leaves the MCP entry alone; the same command with `--no-instructions` added takes them out.
>
> The installer is a shell script for macOS and Linux; read it before you run it.

## Here's how to self-host it

GBrain is MIT-licensed and free to self-host. The recommended start adds memory to the agent you already use and keeps its identity: [Grok Bot](guides/grok-bot.md), [Muse](guides/muse.md), or [Codex / Claude Code](tutorials/connect-coding-agent.md) (`gbrain setup claude-code` or `gbrain setup codex`). An existing hosted brain connects through [harness access](guides/hosted-harness-access.md). A new personal agent with identity files and a private repo uses the [bootstrap guide](guides/bootstrap.md). Read [memory boundaries](guides/memory-boundaries.md) before enabling cloud providers.

The paths below are the manual equivalents. Pick one; mix later if needed.

## 1. Run with an agent platform

Already running [OpenClaw](https://github.com/garrytan/openclaw) or [Hermes](https://github.com/garrytan/hermes)?

```bash
bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable
gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding   # keyless; no server
gbrain skillpack scaffold --harness openclaw --workspace <ws>   # OpenClaw: the five-skill brain-first core
gbrain skillpack scaffold --all       # Hermes or any other workspace: every bundled skill (skills/manifest.json)
gbrain doctor                         # inspect diagnostics and expected empty-brain warnings
```

Scaffolding creates skill files; it does not prove the harness has loaded them.
Connect and verify the intended harness before calling it activated. Entity
capture, recurring jobs and paid enrichment require separate opt-in; none of
the commands above schedules a daily enrichment job.

Scaffolded skills are first-class files in your agent repo — edit freely. To pull upstream gbrain improvements later, `gbrain skillpack reference <name>` diffs your local copy vs the bundle, and `gbrain skillpack reference --all --update-untouched` replaces the skills you never edited (`--dry-run` previews). If your `RESOLVER.md` / `AGENTS.md` still carries the managed `skillpack install` fence, `gbrain skillpack migrate-fence` strips it once and keeps the routing rows inside it.

To upgrade later, use the [memory-only upgrade path](#memory-only-upgrades)
unless services and provider work were deliberately configured. Upgrade runs
schema migrations and post-upgrade work; non-TTY execution is supported and
skips interactive prompts, not all side effects.

## Memory-only upgrades

```bash
GBRAIN_NO_AUTOPILOT_INSTALL=1 GBRAIN_NO_REEMBED=1 gbrain upgrade --no-autopilot-install
```

The autopilot opt-out reaches the migration
orchestrators, and skips existing service-unit rewrites. Other migrations still
run. `GBRAIN_NO_REEMBED=1` independently skips potentially paid reindexing.
The same command upgrades a clone linked with Bun: it fetches, checks the new
release's Bun floor, fast-forwards to the checked commit and runs
`bun install`. Avoid a bare `git pull`, which skips that check. When the new
release needs a newer Bun, `gbrain upgrade` refuses and changes nothing (exit
78): run `bun upgrade`, then the upgrade again
([Bun floor](guides/upgrades-auto-update.md#bun-floor)).
Verify a known keyword result, saved fact and process reopen after upgrading.
See the [agent upgrade steps](../INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md#upgrade).

## 2. CLI standalone

No agent platform, just shell + MCP-aware editor.

```bash
bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable
gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding
```

> **Reinstalled over an existing brain?** The install runs no scripts. The first gbrain command applies schema migrations, and when upgrade migrations are still pending it says so with the command that runs them ([#218](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/issues/218)): `gbrain apply-migrations --yes --no-autopilot-install`. Run `gbrain doctor` if that exits 1. The deterministic fallback is `git clone https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain.git ~/gbrain && cd ~/gbrain && GBRAIN_NO_AUTOPILOT_INSTALL=1 bun install && bun link`.

The init flow detects your repo size and suggests Supabase for brains > 1000 markdown files. Agent-harness installs that want Postgres first can run the ladder instead:

```bash
gbrain init --prefer-postgres    # env URL → Supabase token discovery → local Postgres → opt-in docker → PGLite
```

To switch later:

```bash
gbrain migrate --to postgres --url-env GBRAIN_TARGET_URL --json   # PGLite → Postgres: prints the plan, exits 3
gbrain migrate --to pglite                                        # Postgres → PGLite (rare; brains without write history)
```

The move to Postgres carries the brain's full history and runs after the user approves the plan (`--yes --expect <plan_hash>`). Walkthrough: [Move a PGLite brain to Postgres](guides/move-to-postgres.md).

If Postgres access ever breaks at runtime, `gbrain engine status --probe` diagnoses it and `gbrain db-repair` fixes it — see the "Engine detection and access repair" section of [`docs/ENGINES.md`](ENGINES.md).

For shared / large / multi-machine deployments (a team or company brain with multiple users hitting one server over HTTP MCP with OAuth scoping per user), follow the dedicated walkthrough: **[Tutorial: set up GBrain as your company brain](tutorials/company-brain.md)**.

Optional provider setup: API keys live in `~/.gbrain/config.json` (file plane) or env vars (`VOYAGE_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`). Set them only after choosing the capability and approving its text disclosure and cost. Vendor API keys (and `database_url`/`database_path`) are file-plane routed, so `gbrain config set <KEY> <value>` writes where the pipeline reads it:

```bash
export VOYAGE_API_KEY=pa-...          # default embedding (voyage-4) + reranker (rerank-3-lite) — one key
export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...          # alternative embeddings; also powers automatic fact extraction + chat models
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...   # automatic fact extraction + chat models; also improves search via query expansion
```

For a brain initialized with `--no-embedding`, adding a key alone does not enable
embeddings. Follow the CLI's explicit activation path, for example
`gbrain init --force --embedding-model voyage:voyage-4`, after reviewing the
provider and dimension choice. Keyword retrieval needs none of these keys.

`gbrain config get <key>` redacts secrets and database passwords by default, because its output lands in transcripts and shell history; scripts that need the real value pass `--raw`.

Chat features (automatic fact extraction, enrichment, synthesis, query expansion) use the Anthropic key, else the OpenAI key; other chat providers need a `models.*` pin. With neither key they stay off, and memory comes from agent-authored `## Facts` fences and the `remember` verb.

The autopilot daemon reads keys and process env (`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, proxy vars, custom base URLs) from `~/.gbrain/env`, a 0600 file that `gbrain autopilot --install` creates and bash sources at every daemon start (it honors `GBRAIN_HOME`; shell rc files never reach the daemon). A line there can fetch a key from your secret manager instead of storing it, for example `VOYAGE_API_KEY="$(op read ...)"` (#5196). Re-run `gbrain autopilot --install` after editing it.

To change an existing brain's embedding provider, follow the explicit-consent playbook at [`skills/migrations/v0.46.3.0.md`](../skills/migrations/v0.46.3.0.md), with the full reference in [`docs/guides/embedding-migration.md`](guides/embedding-migration.md). Preview the work and cost before approving a migration; do not repoint existing vectors at a different model.

Common follow-ups:

```bash
gbrain import ~/my-knowledge      # bulk-import a markdown folder
gbrain sync --watch               # live-sync a git repo (autopilot mode)
gbrain autopilot --install        # background daemon for nightly enrichment
```

**Wire this same local brain into your coding agent** — zero server, zero token:

```bash
gbrain setup claude-code   # Claude Code
gbrain setup codex         # Codex
```

The agent spawns `gbrain serve` as a stdio subprocess against your local brain. Setup registers it behind gbrain's launcher (`<gbrain config dir>/hook-launcher/gbrain-hook`), because both harnesses start a stdio server in the session's directory and a script-mode Bun install would otherwise load that directory's `bunfig.toml` and `.env`; `--no-hooks` registers the server without hooks. `--surface starter --advertise verbs` is what every registration gbrain writes: the daily-driver set (40 ops) stays callable, and the tool list shows the seven memory verbs ([MEMORY_VERBS v1](protocol/MEMORY_VERBS_v1.md)) plus `request_tools`, which lists the other tools, returns any tool's full schema and reaches a left-out one. Drop `--advertise verbs` to list the whole starter set, or register `--surface full` (every operation) or `--surface verbs` (only the seven verbs, nothing else callable). Full walkthrough (both this local path and connecting to a remote brain), plus the brain-first protocol to paste into `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`: **[Give your coding agent a memory](tutorials/connect-coding-agent.md)**.

arguments.title: Install Bun and the pinned gbrain CLI
arguments.command:
set -eu
mkdir -p "$HOME/.bun/bin"
case "$(uname -m)" in x86_64) pkg=@oven/bun-linux-x64;; aarch64) pkg=@oven/bun-linux-aarch64;; *) exit 1;; esac
d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/gbrain-bun.XXXXXX)
archive=$(npm pack "$pkg@1.4.5" --pack-destination "$d" --silent)
tar -xzf "$d/$archive" -C "$d" package/bin/bun
